body:
## Summary

The trace work released in JavaScript 0.18.0 is useful checkpoint recording, but continuous recording/replay is not yet complete across initial load, full navigation, or live control-state changes. The current viewer animates a subset of DOM mutations, so it should not yet be described as a complete session animation.

## Confirmed gaps

### No automatic base snapshot

`startTrace()` installs observers and writes `trace.start`, but it does not create an initial checkpoint. A consumer that forgets an immediate `checkpoint()` can produce a continuous trace with mutations and events but no full recovery base.

### Navigation creates an unrecorded interval

The in-page `MutationObserver` belongs to the current document. A full navigation destroys it. The recorder reinstalls it only from `checkpoint()`, so mutations in the new document between navigation and the next checkpoint are not recorded.

The current navigation E2E test checkpoints the new document first and then mutates it. That proves reinstallation after a checkpoint; it does not prove continuous capture through the navigation interval.

### Live state is checkpoint-only

Typing into an input, changing `checked`/`selected`, moving focus, and scrolling commonly change DOM properties without producing attribute mutations. Checkpoints correctly capture this state, but the continuous mutation stream and animation do not. A replay between checkpoints therefore cannot show those user-visible changes.

### Child-list replay is lossy

The viewer currently appends recorded added-element HTML to the target. It does not apply removals and does not preserve the recorded sibling insertion position. Reordering and replace-style updates cannot replay faithfully.

### Correlation identifiers are absent

The portable-format requirements called for browser-context, page, navigation, frame, and action IDs on events. The current timeline does not consistently carry them, which makes multi-page/frame traces ambiguous.

## Expected direction

- Create or require an explicit base checkpoint as part of the `startTrace()` contract; an `initialCheckpoint` option with a safe default would prevent unusable continuous traces.
- Reinstall document observers from navigation lifecycle/init-script hooks, before application code can mutate the new document.
- Record semantic live-state events for controls, focus, and scroll, and apply them in the viewer.
- Encode enough child-list position/removal information for deterministic replay.
- Add stable context/page/navigation/frame/action identities to all relevant records.
- Label the current viewer as partial diagnostic replay until these cases are supported.

## Regression tests

1. Start continuous trace, navigate without an intervening checkpoint, mutate during page initialization, then checkpoint; the initialization mutation must be present.
2. Type, toggle, select, focus, and scroll between checkpoints; stepwise replay must show each state.
3. Insert before a sibling, move a node, remove a node, and replace a subtree; replay must match the final checkpoint DOM.
4. Record two pages and an iframe concurrently; every event must resolve to an unambiguous owner.
title: Continuous trace replay is incomplete across navigation and live state
